 Lakers face tough long-term decision between Ziaire Williams, Matisse Thybulle 
 You can't go wrong, unless you rule out keeping both! By Colin Keane | Nov 17, 2026, 1:00 PM EST Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source Ziaire Williams. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Los Angeles Lakers general manager Rob Pelinka totally cooked by acquiring both Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams on minimum deals this past offseason.
--> Los Angeles Lakers general manager Rob Pelinka totally cooked by acquiring both Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams on minimum deals this past offseason.
 Both Thybulle and Williams are perfect fits on this Luka Doncic-led Lakers group, and it's already at the point where it's tough to see either player not being a part of this group moving forward.
--> Both Thybulle and Williams are perfect fits on this Luka Doncic-led Lakers group, and it's already at the point where it's tough to see either player not being a part of this group moving forward.
 Of course, with both guys on one-year deals expiring after 2026-27, the Lakers are at risk of losing one or both of them. That leads to the question: who between Thybulle and Williams should be considered more of a priority for the Lakers to lock up long-term? There's a case to be made in either direction.

That leads to the question: who between Thybulle and Williams should be considered more of a priority for the Lakers to lock up long-term? There's a case to be made in either direction.
 Who should the Lakers choose between Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams (if they had to)?
--> Who should the Lakers choose between Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams (if they had to)?
 The case for Thybulle
--> The case for Thybulle
 Thybulle is in his athletic prime right now, and it'd be tough to argue that he's not a superior defender to Williams at this point in time. Thybulle's length, active hands, and general defensive instincts allow him to get a ton of steals, and he's become an absolutely essential element of LA's best lineup. I haven't even mentioned that he's shooting the ball with confidence and has become a consistent threat from 3 beside Luka.

--> If you need to win a game tonight, you might roll with Thybulle over Williams based on the immediacy of his value. But then again, we're talking about a long-term deal here, which leads us to the advantage that Williams has in this conversation...
 The case for Williams
--> The case for Williams
 Williams, still only 25, hasn't reached his ceiling. There have been times this season when he's looked like the Lakers' fourth-most-valuable player outside of the Big 3. He has a lot more offensive upside than Thybulle does, and he's also a good outside shooter. 
--> Williams, still only 25, hasn't reached his ceiling. There have been times this season when he's looked like the Lakers' fourth-most-valuable player outside of the Big 3. He has a lot more offensive upside than Thybulle does, and he's also a good outside shooter. 
 Williams' durability history would be slightly concerning if you were mulling a long-term deal. But since other suitors would surely be willing to fork over a big payday to secure Ziaire's services, the Lakers would have to take on that risk and pay up if they wanted to keep him on the squad beyond this season.
--> Williams' durability history would be slightly concerning if you were mulling a long-term deal. But since other suitors would surely be willing to fork over a big payday to secure Ziaire's services, the Lakers would have to take on that risk and pay up if they wanted to keep him on the squad beyond this season.
 Why not both?
--> Why not both?
 It sounds like a cop out, but I truly believe the Lakers need to do whatever it takes to keep both Thybulle and Williams beyond 2026-27. It'll be up to Pelinka to work his magic and retain both guys at reasonable numbers. If anything, I could see Williams getting poached by someone else on a bold overpay, given his youth and upside. It's a good thing, in that event, that the Lakers could still realistically bring back both Thybulle and Jake LaRavia.
